title: Fix idempotency key race condition in job store
description:
**Bug**: `core/infra/memory/job_store.go:924-977` — `TryAcquireLock` uses non-transactional `SetNX`. The check for legacy key and setting of scoped key is not atomic, allowing two concurrent requests with the same idempotency key to both succeed.

**Fix**: Use a Lua script or Redis WATCH-MULTI-EXEC to make the check-and-set atomic.

**Files**: `core/infra/memory/job_store.go`
definitionOfDone: Idempotency key check-and-set is atomic (Lua or WATCH/MULTI)
Concurrent test proves no duplicate acquisition

implementationPlan.description:
Replace the non-atomic legacy-check + SetNX in TrySetIdempotencyKeyScoped (job_store.go:947-975) with a Lua script that atomically checks both legacy and scoped keys:

```go
const idempotencyScript = `
local legacyKey = KEYS[1]
local scopedKey = KEYS[2]
local jobID = ARGV[1]
local ttl = tonumber(ARGV[2])

-- Check legacy key first
local legacy = redis.call("GET", legacyKey)
if legacy and legacy ~= false then
  return legacy  -- Return existing job ID
end

-- Atomic check-and-set on scoped key
local ok = redis.call("SET", scopedKey, jobID, "NX", "PX", ttl)
if ok then
  return "OK:" .. jobID
end
local existing = redis.call("GET", scopedKey)
return existing or ""
`
```

Parse the result: if it starts with "OK:" it's a new acquisition; otherwise it's the existing job ID.
Update the Go code to call the Lua script instead of separate Redis commands. Handle the tenant-based routing (empty tenant uses simple SetNX, non-empty tenant uses Lua script with legacy key check).
Run `go test ./core/infra/memory/...` to verify no regressions. Add a concurrent test that submits two requests with the same idempotency key simultaneously and verifies only one succeeds.
